standard_prerequisites.name: The criterion for universal injectivity by testing with finite modules
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, label algebra-theorem-universally-exact-criteria, invoked at proof line 2080
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces universal injectivity of the map into the completion to the injectivity of the map after tensoring with an arbitrary finite module over the base.

standard_prerequisites.name: A module injects into the product of its localisations at its associated primes, and an intersection of powers of an ideal vanishes under a condition
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, labels algebra-lemma-zero-at-ass-zero (proof line 2091) and algebra-lemma-intersect-powers-ideal-module-zero (proof line 2099)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first lets the vanishing of the kernel be checked at the associated primes, and the second shows that the intersection of the powers of the ideal inside the localisation vanishes because the extended ideal is contained in a prime.

core_obligations: Reduce to the injectivity statement: by the universal injectivity criterion it suffices to show that the map is injective after tensoring with an arbitrary finite module, and since the tensor product of the completion receives a canonical map from the completion of the tensor product it suffices to prove injectivity of the map from the module into its own completion (proof lines 2077-2085).

Reduce to the associated primes: the kernel is the intersection of the powers of the ideal, and since the module injects into the product of its localisations at the associated primes it suffices to show that the localisation of the kernel at every associated prime vanishes (proof lines 2087-2091).

Conclude: for an associated prime the hypothesis provides a prime containing the extended ideal plus that prime, the localisation of the kernel at the given prime is a localisation of the one at that prime, and there the intersection of the powers of the extended ideal vanishes by the intersection statement (proof lines 2092-2099).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to injectivity of the map into the completion (proof lines 2077-2085).
Reduce to the localisations at the associated primes (proof lines 2087-2091).
Use the hypothesis to find a prime where the intersection of powers vanishes (proof lines 2092-2099).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that under a condition on the associated primes of the tensor products with finite modules, the map from a finite module into its adic completion is universally injective over the base (statement lines 2059-2075, tag 05DL). The proof reduces the universal injectivity to injectivity, then to the vanishing of the localisations of the kernel at the associated primes of the module, and finally uses the hypothesis to find a prime containing the extended ideal and the associated prime, where the intersection of the powers of the ideal vanishes by the corresponding statement for modules. The reduction to the associated primes is the substance, so the claim is H2.
